Question: Jiffy denture is a type of
Explanation:

Currently, there are two popular types of immediate dentures:
• Conventional or classic immediate denture (CID): After this immediate denture is placed and after healing is completed, the denture is refitted or relined to serve as the long-term prosthesis.
• Interim or transitional immediate denture (IID): After this immediate denture is made and after healing is completed, a second, new complete denture is fabricated as the long-term prosthesis.

An abbreviated type of IID has been called as 'Jiffy Denture'. Jiffy denture differs from the IID in that the denture 'teeth' are usually made with tooth-colored, autopolymerizing acrylic resin or portions of the patient's preexisting fixed or removable partial denture(s). The main disadvantage of 'jiffy dentures' is that the materials used are not as long lasting (e.g., in wear and color stability) as conventional denture teeth and processed bases.

The lamellar bone (highly organized) is the one with higher resistance and modulus of elasticity, being the ideal bone for the load support.

Question: Fracture of denture at midline, reason is:
Explanation:
'B' [Journal of Indian prosthodontic society / july 2009 / Vol. 9 / issue 3]

The midline fracture of the maxillary complete denture is the fracture most commonly seen in dentures. This is largely because as the ridges resorb and remodel, the palatal bone does not. This leads to a high-centering of the denture, where the denture contacts primarily in the hard palate and secondarily contacts the residual ridge. This results in a constant rocking effect which accelerates bone loss and causes a steady loss of stability of the denture, in time leading to a stress fracture of the denture base. Poor fit was the prime cause in upper denture fracture, such dentures flex in the mouth during function around the midline and due to repeated small loading during mastication lead to the fatigue fracture.

Question: Which of these is a medio-lateral curvature
Explanation:
'A' [Check Explanation Below]

• Curve of Spee (Anteroposterior curve): It is a curved alignment of the occlusal surfaces of the teeth following the arc of a circle of about 4 inches radius, with the center above the eye.
• Curve of Wilson (Mediolateral curve): It is the mediolateral curvature of the posterior occlusal plane. For each side of arch the mandibular posterior teeth are tilted lingually, and the maxillary posterior teeth are tilted buccally.
• Curve of Monson: It is based on the spherical theory. Each cusp and incisal edge touches or conforms to the surface of a sphere of 8 inches diameter with its center in the region of the glabella.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: In case of complete dentures with shallow angle of eminence, the type of teeth used to obtain balanced occlusion is:
Explanation:
'D' [Okeson 6th ed 114]

Posterior tooth form and condylar angle:
• Shallow eminence angle → requires shallow cuspal teeth (short cusps with shallow fossae) so that balanced occlusion can be achieved without steep compensating curves.
• Steep eminence angle → allows teeth with deep cusps and fossae.
• This principle follows from Thielemann's formula: compensating curves and cuspal height must be balanced with condylar inclination.

Question: Sunderland classification type IV nerve injury which structure is intact
Explanation:
'A' [Check Explanation Below]

Sunderland Classification of Nerve Injuries:
| Class | Injury | Structures Intact |
|---|---|---|
| I (Neuropraxia) | No axon disruption | Endoneurium, Perineurium, Epineurium all intact |
| II | Axonal disruption | Endoneurium, Perineurium, Epineurium intact |
| III | Axonal + Endoneurial disruption | Perineurium, Epineurium intact |
| IV | Perineurial rupture/fascicle disruption | Epineurium intact |
| V (Neurotmesis) | Complete nerve trunk discontinuity | Nothing intact |

Sunderland Type IV: Epineurium is the only intact structure.

Question: Which of the following statements is true regarding taking interocclusal record with plaster of Paris?
Option A: It shows resistance to interocclusal force
Option C: Abrasion of plaster with movement of articulator
Option D: It is difficult for the patient to keep mandible at desired position for long time till setting of plaster
Explanation:
'D' [Interocclusal records in prosthodontic rehabilitations - An overview - Dr. Neeraj Arora]

Disadvantages of plaster of Paris for interocclusal records:
• It is difficult to handle because the material is fluid and unmanageable prior to setting.
• The final interocclusal record is brittle.
• It dehydrates, is significantly brittle, sticks to the teeth and is technique sensitive.
• It is difficult for the patient to keep mandible at desired position for long time till setting of plaster.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Most common area of fracture of maxillary denture:
Explanation:
'D' [AV Naik, Complete denture fractures; an overview]

Midline fracture was most common in both upper and lower dentures. Anteroposterior direction including labial notch (midline) is the most common site of fracture of maxillary denture.

• The two types of forces can be applied on the palatal plate of the denture, the compressive and tensile forces.
• During the loading cycle, the tensile and compressive stresses are generated in the acrylic resin denture.
• Midline fracture occurs when the area around the labial notch acts as a stress concentrator with crack initiation and propagation.
• The crack always propagates toward the area of least resistance, which is the shortest distance between the notch and the posterior border of the acrylic resin - i.e. the midline.

Question: The following is not done during pre-prosthetic mouth preparation:
Explanation:

Pre-prosthetic MOUTH preparation includes:
• Removal of residual roots and impacted teeth
• Removal of bony irregularities

Question: All are common between denture sore mouth and burning mouth syndrome except?
Option B: Prevalence is more in Females than male
Option D: more prevalence in denture bearing patients
Explanation:
'C' [Boucher 12th ed 35]

Burning mouth syndrome (BMS) and denture stomatitis comparison:
• Both are more common in elderly patients (Option A is common).
• Both are more common in females (Option B is common).

Question: Saliva under denture base providing adequate retention is an example of
Explanation:
'A' [Heartwell, textbook of complete denture 5th ed]

Adhesion is the attraction between saliva molecules and denture base and oral mucosa. Cohesion is the attraction between saliva molecules to each other. Interfacial surface tension is the result of the interaction of adhesion and cohesion.

Question: Maximum retention in soft palate is seen when
Option A: V-shape palate with 60 degrees to horizontal
Option C: Broader coverage of palate with almost zero angle
Explanation:
'C' [Winkler 2nd ed 48]

Retention of the maxillary denture is dependent on palatal form. A flat palate (broader coverage, almost zero angle of soft palate inclination) provides the maximum seal/retention because:
• Greater surface area for adhesion
• Wider posterior palatal seal
• No displacement of denture in any direction

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Higher broader coverage of denture base is explained by
Explanation:
'C' [Heartwell, Textbook of complete denture 5th ed 227]

Maximum coverage provides the snowshoe effect - the same as snow shoes which distribute weight across a broad area. In denture construction, maximum coverage of the denture base helps spread occlusal forces over a greater surface area of the ridge, reducing the stress per unit area on the tissues.

Subject: Complete Denture
Question: Most common difficulty seen when mandibular complete denture with acrylic teeth opposes natural teeth
Option D: Difficulty in establishing balance occlusion bilaterally
Explanation:
'D' [Winkler 2nd ed 417]

Single complete denture opposing natural dentition has the following challenges:
• Unfavorable occlusal relationships
• Difficulty in achieving balanced occlusion bilaterally since natural teeth do not provide balanced contacts
• If porcelain teeth are used, there will be excessive wear of the opposing natural teeth.
• If acrylic teeth are used, they will wear rapidly against natural teeth.

Question: Disadvantage of metallic denture base
Explanation:
'C' [Winkler 2nd ed 313 / McCracken]

A metal denture base's principal disadvantages are that it is difficult to adjust and reline. Also it cannot be relined with direct (chairside) reline materials without first removing a portion of the metal base.

Question: Denture stomatitis is commonly caused by?
Explanation:

Question: Use of transparent acrylic template in case of immediate denture helps in:
Explanation:
'A' [Winkler 2nd ed 71]

Identification of the amount and extent of bone to be removed can be simplified by the fabrication of a transparent template made on a previously altered cast. The bone prominences and irregularities are indicated in the patient's mouth by pressing the template against the mucosa of the extraction site. These areas of bone can then be surgically reduced.

Question: Difference between Hanau Vue and Hanau Vue II is

Question: Anterior guidance cannot be used in following cases except?
Option C: Class 1 with severe class anterior open bite
Explanation:

Question: When soft tissue liner is used, pressure threshold for basal tissues should?
Option D: depends on basal tissue area resiliency
Explanation:
'C' [A technique for using short term soft liners as definitive soft liners - The Journal of Contemporary Dental Practice]

It does not change the pressure threshold for basal tissue. Soft liners act as shock absorbers but do not alter the intrinsic pressure threshold of the underlying basal tissues.

Question: After getting new denture, patient complaints of tiredness while wearing it, while tiredness got relieved on removing the denture, what will be the cause?
Explanation:
'A' [Winkler 2nd ed 190]

A lack of interocclusal distance or increased vertical dimension of occlusion can create soreness of underlying ridges, muscle fatigue, and temporomandibular joint pain. Muscle will continue to exert force to overcome this obstacle, hence patient will complaint of tiredness while wearing it. The tiredness will be relieved on removing the denture as the muscles can relax.

Question: A polysulfide impression was taken and cast was poured from it, impression was good, but details have not come, what to do
Option B: Add surfactant to the impression material
Option C: Spray surfactant on the cast and wash the impression before pouring
Option D: Add surfactant to both cast and impression material
Explanation:
'B' [The Journal of Prosthetic Dentistry - Wettability of elastomeric impression materials]

The incorporation of certain nonionic surfactants into silicone and polysulfide elastomers increases their wettability. Improved wettability results in less bubble entrapment in poured casts and better surface detail reproduction. Adding surfactant to the impression material (before taking the impression) improves wettability and allows better detail.
